item.title: Edition #2: Apple's AI Siri Targets March Launch; LeCun Leaves Meta for World Models; February Breaks AI Investment Records
item.description: Apple's reimagined Siri targets a March launch powered by Google's Gemini model. Yann LeCun leaves Meta to build a world models startup at a 3 billion euro valuation. Anthropic launches enterprise plug-ins for finance and HR. Nvidia's Vera Rubin enters production. February closes as the biggest month in AI investment history with $195B+ in capital. Apple teases iPhone 17e and budget MacBook for March 4.
item.content:encoded:
Today's Blast — 6 Stories

1. Apple's AI-Powered Siri Targets March Launch — With Google's Gemini Under the Hood

Apple's completely reimagined Siri is targeting a March release alongside iOS 26.4, powered by Google's 1.2-trillion-parameter Gemini model in a deal worth roughly $1 billion per year. The new assistant will be context-aware, capable of on-screen actions and cross-app workflows — though Bloomberg reports some features may slip to a later update.

Source: MacRumors · Read more →

2. Yann LeCun Leaves Meta to Build €3 Billion "World Models" Startup

After 12 years at Meta, legendary AI scientist Yann LeCun has departed to launch AMI Labs, raising €500 million at a €3 billion valuation. The Paris-based startup is a contrarian bet that "world models" — AI that understands physics rather than just predicting text — are the real path to intelligent machines.

Source: MIT Technology Review · Read more →

3. Anthropic Launches AI Plug-ins for Wall Street, HR, and Design

Anthropic unveiled 10 new plug-ins for its Claude platform, built with partners including FactSet, LSEG, Salesforce, and DocuSign. Financial advisors can now automate portfolio analysis and rebalancing, while HR teams can streamline hiring workflows.

Source: Bloomberg · Read more →

4. Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI Platform Enters Full Production — 5x Faster Than Blackwell

Nvidia announced that its next-generation Vera Rubin AI chip platform is now in full production, promising five times the performance of the current Blackwell architecture. The platform is optimized for agentic AI and mixture-of-experts models, with partner products shipping in the second half of 2026.

Source: Nvidia Newsroom · Read more →

5. February Closes as the Biggest Month in AI Investment History — $195B+

February 2026 wrapped with an estimated $195 billion or more in tracked AI capital — easily the most consequential month in venture finance history. The headliners: OpenAI's $110 billion mega-round, Anthropic's $30 billion Series G, and Waymo's $16 billion raise.

Source: TechCrunch · Read more →

6. Apple Teases "Big Week" — iPhone 17e and Budget MacBook Coming March 4

Apple CEO Tim Cook hinted at a "big week ahead" with media events planned in New York, Shanghai, and London on March 4. Expectations include the iPhone 17e, an all-new budget MacBook, and refreshes to the Mac Studio and Studio Display — all powered by Apple's latest M5 chips.

Source: MacRumors · Read more →

item.title: Edition #1: OpenAI Closes Record $110B Round; Pentagon Bans Anthropic; Block Cuts Half Its Staff
item.description: Launch edition! OpenAI closes the largest private funding round in history at $110B. The Pentagon bans Anthropic after a standoff over military AI guardrails. Block cuts nearly half its workforce in an AI bet. Meta rents Google TPU chips. Perplexity launches multi-agent "Computer." Google commits $1B to iron-air batteries. UN creates AI advisory panel.
item.content:encoded:
Today's Blast — 7 Stories

1. OpenAI Closes Record $110B Funding Round, Now Valued at $840 Billion

OpenAI has closed the largest private funding round in history — $110 billion anchored by Amazon's $50B commitment, plus $30B each from Nvidia and SoftBank. At $840 billion post-money, OpenAI is now valued above almost every public company on Earth.

Source: TechCrunch · Read more →

2. Pentagon Bans Anthropic After High-Stakes Military AI Standoff

The Trump administration ordered all federal agencies to stop using Anthropic's AI after the company refused to drop its guardrails on lethal autonomous weapons and mass surveillance. Anthropic held firm, saying "threats do not change our position."

Source: Washington Post · Read more →

3. Block Cuts Nearly Half Its Workforce as Jack Dorsey Bets Big on AI

Jack Dorsey's fintech company laid off about 4,000 employees — nearly half its staff — citing AI-driven efficiency gains. Dorsey predicted most companies will make similar cuts within a year. Block's stock surged 24%.

Source: CNN · Read more →

4. Meta Signs Multi-Billion Dollar Deal to Rent Google's TPU Chips

Meta has signed a multi-year agreement to rent Google's custom TPU chips for AI training — signaling that demand for AI compute is so intense that even the biggest buyers are diversifying beyond Nvidia.

Source: SiliconANGLE · Read more →

5. Perplexity Launches "Computer" — An AI Agent That Runs Other AI Agents

Perplexity's new system treats Claude, Gemini, GPT-5.2, Grok, and others like specialized employees on a shared team. Describe an outcome and Computer breaks it into tasks, spawns sub-agents, and runs them in parallel.

Source: TechCrunch · Read more →

6. Google Drops $1B on Form Energy's 100-Hour Iron-Air Battery

Google committed $1 billion to deploy the world's largest battery — a 300 MW iron-air system that can deliver continuous power for 100 hours — at a Minnesota data center.

Source: TechCrunch · Read more →

7. UN Creates International AI Advisory Panel With 40 Members From 37 Nations

The United Nations General Assembly approved a 40-member scientific AI advisory panel to serve as an "early-warning system and evidence engine" for AI policy worldwide.

Source: Nature · Read more →
